area.text: Back in the lab, with all our fingers. Lovely. Open your field log. Multiply each station's width by its depth to find its cross-sectional area.

discharge.text: Those are our areas. Now multiply each area by the water velocity at that station. That gives discharge in cubic metres per second.

total.text: Three stations, one stream. Add the three station discharges shown on the glass board. Two decimal places are plenty, and a little rounding is allowed.

complete.text: We did it! Prehistoric streamflow data, and a discharge we can explain. Science survives another field trip.

area_hint1.text: Check your field log first. Use the width and depth from the same station.

area_hint2.text: Area is width times depth. Multiply the two measurements, then check where your decimal point belongs.

discharge_hint1.text: Use the area you've just calculated, and the velocity recorded for that same station.

discharge_hint2.text: Multiply square metres by metres per second. Your answer describes a volume of water passing each second.

total_hint1.text: Add the three station discharges on the glass board. This time, we're adding, not multiplying.

total_hint2.text: Line up the decimal points. Add all three station discharges shown on the board. Keep two decimal places.
